engines.name: 3.0L supercharged V6 hybrid (S Hybrid, S E-Hybrid)
3.0L turbo V6 plug-in hybrid (E-Hybrid, S E-Hybrid)
4.0L twin-turbo V8 (Turbo, GTS, Turbo GT, S)
4.0L twin-turbo V8 plug-in hybrid (Turbo S E-Hybrid, Turbo E-Hybrid)

issues.t: Plastic coolant pipes under the intake crack and leak
issues.sym: Coolant on the ground under the middle of the engine, a sweet smell, steam from the engine bay, a low-coolant warning or the temperature gauge climbing fast.
issues.why: The V8 engines in the first Cayenne route coolant through plastic pipes that sit in the hot valley under the intake manifold. After years of heat they turn brittle and split, often with little warning.
issues.next: Stop driving if the temperature rises; running hot can wreck the engine. Have the pipes replaced with the aluminum upgrade kit, which means removing the intake. If you're buying one, ask for proof this was done.

issues.t: Driveshaft center support bearing fails and clunks
issues.sym: A clunk or thump when pulling away or shifting between drive and reverse, vibration through the floor at speed, or a wobble from the middle of the car.
issues.why: The long driveshaft to the rear axle is held in the middle by a bearing in a rubber mount. The rubber splits with age, letting the shaft move around, and the bearing itself can wear out.
issues.next: Get it inspected soon. If only the rubber support has failed, it can be replaced on its own; if the joints or bearing are worn, the shaft may need replacing. A shaft that breaks can damage other parts.

issues.t: Transfer case clutch wears, causing jerky or lurching acceleration
issues.sym: Surging or uneven acceleration, mostly in 2nd and 3rd gear, shudder in tight low-speed turns, or a crackling noise from under the car. It can show up as early as 15,000 miles.
issues.why: The transfer case sends power to the front wheels through a clutch pack. Its 'lifetime' fluid breaks down with heat, and water or mismatched tire sizes add to clutch slip, so the clutch starts to grab and slip.
issues.next: Have a Porsche specialist confirm it's the transfer case and not misfires or the transmission. A fluid change sometimes helps; otherwise the unit is replaced. Keep all four tires the same size and wear.

issues.t: Ignition coils fail and cause misfires
issues.sym: Check engine light (often flashing), a rough idle, shaking under acceleration or a sudden loss of power.
issues.why: The coil packs on these engines crack and weaken with heat and age. Once one goes, the others are usually not far behind.
issues.next: Don't drive far with a flashing check engine light; it can overheat the catalytic converters. Have the misfiring cylinder found; many owners replace all the coils, and plugs, at once.

issues.t: Cylinder bore scoring in the V8
issues.sym: Rising oil use, a ticking or knocking noise (piston slap) especially when cold, blue smoke, and black soot on one bank's tailpipe more than the other.
issues.why: On some 4.5L and 4.8L V8 engines, the cylinder walls get scratched by the pistons, so the rings no longer seal. It's often found at higher mileage.
issues.next: Have a borescope inspection done to look inside the cylinders. If scoring is confirmed, the fix is a rebuild with new cylinder liners or a replacement engine, which is a major repair.

issues.t: Fuel pump flange cracks and leaks fuel (recall)
issues.sym: A strong smell of gasoline, especially near the rear seats, or fuel dripping under the car.
issues.why: The plastic flange on top of the fuel pump can crack over time and let fuel leak out, which creates a fire risk.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, don't park in a garage and get it to a dealer. Recall 17V576000 replaces the flanges with protected ones for free.

issues.t: Shifter bushing can let the car roll away (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter shows Park and the key comes out, but the transmission isn't really in Park. The car can roll when you walk away.
issues.why: A bushing that links the gear lever to the transmission cable can wear and pop off, so the lever and transmission no longer agree.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake until it's fixed. Recall 19V446000 replaces the shifter cable bushing for free.

issues.t: Transfer case housing could starve gears of oil (recall)
issues.sym: Whining or grinding from the transfer case, and eventual failure of the four-wheel-drive unit.
issues.why: A change to the transfer case housing casting could let the internal oil pump turn in its bore, cutting oil supply to the gears.
issues.next: Confirm with a dealer that the inspection was done. The recall replaced the transfer case where needed.

issues.t: Fuel pump failure causes long cranking or stalling
issues.sym: The engine takes a long time to start, starts and then dies, stumbles under acceleration, or eventually won't start at all.
issues.why: The in-tank fuel pumps wear and overheat with age. On direct-injection engines from 2008 on, the high-pressure pump on the engine can also fail.
issues.next: Have fuel pressure tested so the right pump is replaced. Avoid running the tank very low, which makes the in-tank pumps run hotter.

issues.t: Airbag light from loose seat airbag connectors
issues.sym: The airbag (SRS) warning light comes on, sometimes on and off, often after the seats are moved.
issues.why: The wiring plugs for the side airbags under the front seats can lose contact. NHTSA investigated after thousands of warranty claims, and Porsche changed the connectors in later builds.
issues.next: Have the airbag fault codes read. Ask a dealer whether the free connector modification for cars built through November 2004 was done on your car.

issues.t: Air suspension compressor wears out
issues.sym: An 'air suspension' warning, the car slow to rise or stuck low, or the compressor running loudly or for a long time.
issues.why: The compressor that pumps up the air springs works harder as it ages and as small leaks develop. Worn seals inside are a common cause.
issues.next: Have the system checked for leaks first; a leak will kill a new compressor. A seal kit or an aftermarket compressor is another option besides a dealer unit.

issues.t: Air spring or strut leaks and the car sags
issues.sym: One corner sits low after parking, an air suspension warning, a harsher ride, or popping and creaking from the suspension.
issues.why: The rubber air bags in each strut crack with age and cold weather, and the top seals and O-rings can leak. Some newer cars have had leaks from faulty strut welds or bellows.
issues.next: Have the leak found before replacing parts. Many owners replace the struts in pairs. Driving long on a leaking strut wears out the compressor.

issues.t: Steering lock fault stops the car from starting
issues.sym: A 'Steering faulty' message and the car won't start or respond, often without warning.
issues.why: The electronic steering column lock used with the keyless (KESSY) system can fail, and the car won't start unless it unlocks.
issues.next: Have the fault codes read by a Porsche specialist. The factory fix is a new column lock part with coding to the immobilizer; some shops offer repairs for less.

issues.t: Water leaks from blocked drains damage electronics
issues.sym: Wet carpets, water sloshing in the doors or footwells, a damp smell, or random electrical faults after rain.
issues.why: Drains for the sunroof, the area below the windshield and the A/C box clog with leaves and dirt. Water then backs up into the cabin, where control modules and wiring sit low.
issues.next: Clear the drains and dry the car quickly. Have any wet modules checked before they corrode. A 2015-2023 sunroof class settlement has closed for claims.

issues.t: Brake booster failure from water getting in
issues.sym: A brake booster warning, a hard brake pedal or longer stopping distances.
issues.why: On early 957 and 958 models, water could get into the brake booster area and damage it.
issues.next: Have the brakes checked right away; don't rely on the car until the booster works. Clearing the drains helps prevent it coming back.

issues.t: Camshaft adjuster or solenoid fault causes rough idle
issues.sym: Rough idle, hesitation and a check engine light with camshaft timing or valve-lift codes.
issues.why: The variable cam timing and valve-lift parts on the 4.8L V8 rely on solenoids and adjusters that can fail or get dirty oil. A failed solenoid is a common cause.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the solenoid wiring and oil level checked. Keeping up with oil changes helps.

issues.t: Carbon buildup on intake valves
issues.sym: Rough idle, misfires, hesitation and loss of power, slowly getting worse over many miles.
issues.why: Direct-injection engines spray fuel straight into the cylinders, so nothing washes the intake valves. Oil vapor bakes onto them and restricts airflow.
issues.next: Have a shop confirm it with a scope. The usual fix is walnut-shell blasting of the intake valves.

issues.t: Harsh downshifts from the Tiptronic valve body
issues.sym: Hard or clunky downshifts, sometimes with a bang, delayed shifts or a rough feel in stop-and-go driving.
issues.why: Wear and sticking valves in the automatic's valve body, or old fluid, affect how smoothly it shifts.
issues.next: Start with a scan for codes, a software check and a fluid change. Only replace the valve body if testing points to it.

issues.t: Timing chain wear on the VR6 engine
issues.sym: A rattle for a few seconds after a cold start, a check engine light with cam timing codes, or rough running.
issues.why: The timing chains and guides on the narrow-angle V6 stretch and wear with miles, especially past about 100,000 miles or with long oil intervals.
issues.next: Have the cam timing values checked. If the chain is stretched, replace it before it jumps a tooth and damages the valves.

issues.t: Coolant leaks from thermostat housing and crossover pipes
issues.sym: Slowly dropping coolant level, a sweet smell, drips under the front or back of the engine, or a low coolant warning.
issues.why: On the 957 V8, a glued pipe at the thermostat housing can slip out and the rear coolant crossover connections can leak. Porsche later made a threaded version.
issues.next: Have the cooling system pressure-tested to find the leak. Don't keep topping up for long; a sudden failure can overheat the engine.

issues.t: Water pump leaks or fails
issues.sym: Coolant leaking at the front of the engine, a whining or grinding noise from the belt area, or overheating.
issues.why: The water pump's seal and bearing wear out. Owners report it among the more common repairs.
issues.next: Replace it at the first sign of leaking. Many owners replace the thermostat at the same time.

issues.t: Camshaft adjuster bolts can break (recall)
issues.sym: Rough running, a check engine light with cam timing codes, rattling, or in the worst case the engine stalls or is badly damaged.
issues.why: Bolts holding the camshaft adjusters together on the 2011 V8 could loosen and break.
issues.next: Check that recall 17V368000 is done. It replaces the bolts and, if needed, the adjusters for free.

issues.t: Brake pedal pivot pin clip may be missing (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels loose or out of place.
issues.why: Some cars left the factory without the circlip that holds the pedal's pivot pin, so the pedal could come off its mount.
issues.next: Don't drive with a loose brake pedal. Recall 16V169000 inspects and fits the clip for free.

issues.t: Turbo turbine wheel can fracture (recall)
issues.sym: Loss of power, smoke from the exhaust, and in rare cases fire.
issues.why: A casting defect could make the turbine wheel break, which can draw oil into the exhaust.
issues.next: Recall 12V329000 replaces the turbine wheels for free on affected Cayenne Turbo models.

issues.t: S Hybrid fuel rail can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A smell of gasoline from the engine bay.
issues.why: The fuel injection system on some Cayenne S Hybrid models could leak fuel, creating a fire risk.
issues.next: Recall 15V016000 replaces the fuel rails for free.

issues.t: PCM infotainment screen freezes or keeps restarting
issues.sym: The center screen goes blank, freezes, reboots while driving, or takes a long time to load, taking navigation, audio and the camera with it.
issues.why: Software faults in the Porsche Communication Management unit are common across generations. Sometimes the unit itself fails.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for software updates first. If the unit keeps rebooting after that, it may need replacing.

issues.t: S E-Hybrid high-voltage battery or controller fault
issues.sym: Hybrid system warnings, reduced or no electric range, charging that stops, or a red warning with clicking from the rear.
issues.why: The high-voltage battery system, its controller and its cooling pump can fault. A weak 12V battery can also trigger these warnings on this model.
issues.next: Test the 12V battery first. Porsche extended coverage on the battery controller for these years, so ask a dealer before paying.

issues.t: Power tailgate motor or struts fail
issues.sym: The power liftgate won't open or close, stops partway, or drifts down and won't stay up.
issues.why: The tailgate motors and gas struts wear out over time, and cold weather makes weak struts worse.
issues.next: Don't stand under a tailgate that won't stay up. Replacing worn struts or the motor usually fixes it.

issues.t: Fuel line connector can leak in the engine bay (recall)
issues.sym: A smell of gasoline from under the hood.
issues.why: The quick-connect fitting on a fuel line in the engine compartment could leak near hot parts, creating a fire risk.
issues.next: Recall 20V270000 replaces the fuel line and connector for free.

issues.t: Cracks in V8 cylinder bores (recall)
issues.sym: Oil leaks, a stall or engine damage.
issues.why: Cracks could form in the cylinder bore surfaces of some 4.0L V8 engines.
issues.next: Recall 21V341000 replaces the engine for free on affected cars.

issues.t: Rear trailing arm lock nut can break (recall)
issues.sym: The car pulls or handles oddly, or tires wear unevenly.
issues.why: A lock nut on the rear trailing arm could crack from stress corrosion and let the rear axle move out of alignment. A follow-up recall checks the alignment on repaired cars.
issues.next: Recalls 21V271000 and 22V040000 replace the nuts and check alignment for free, including replacing unevenly worn tires.

issues.t: Home charging cable can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: The plug or wall outlet gets hot or smells like burning while charging on a 240V outlet.
issues.why: The 220/240V charging cable can overheat the outlet or itself near full charge.
issues.next: Stop using the 240V cable until a dealer supplies the replacement cable with a temperature sensor under recall 23V841000. Have an electrician check any scorched outlet.

issues.t: Rearview camera image may not appear (recall)
issues.sym: The screen stays blank or is slow to show the camera picture when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: A software fault in the driver-assistance system can stop or delay the camera image.
issues.next: Use the mirrors carefully until a dealer installs the free software update (recalls 19V111000 and 25V896000).

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump may not be tightened properly (recall)
issues.sym: A smell of fuel from the engine bay or a fuel leak.
issues.why: Fasteners on the engine's high-pressure fuel pump may not have been tightened enough at the factory.
issues.next: Recall 25V634000 inspects and tightens the pump and replaces it and the lines where needed, free of charge.

issues.t: 12V battery drains and the car won't start
issues.sym: The car is dead after sitting a day or two, or several random warning lights come on at once.
issues.why: Newer Cayennes have many control units that can stay awake and drain the 12V battery. Some models use a lithium battery that disconnects itself to protect itself, and battery sensor campaigns exist.
issues.next: Have the battery tested and a parasitic drain test done before replacing parts. Use a battery maintainer if the car sits.
